messages.subject: Time limit and visual options
parts:
Hi Phil and everyone,

I created a test via mirtCAT. There are 2 problems, I need your help,

1- I want to save item response time for each item, in forced choice test. In output, all item_time are 0. I can obtain item response time only when I set df$Timer,  but in this case test is not forced choice. Is it possible to save item response time in a forced choice test.

2- Some of items contain picture. I can add picture to item stem, as you show in github examples. But when I try to add picture in options, it does not work. Is it possible to add picture in options?

Thanks,

Levent

messages.subject: Re: Time limit and visual options
parts: On Wed, Mar 9, 2022 at 9:22 AM leven...@gmail.com <leven...@gmail.com> wrote:

Hi Phil and everyone,

I created a test via mirtCAT. There are 2 problems, I need your help,

1- I want to save item response time for each item, in forced choice test. In output, all item_time are 0. I can obtain item response time only when I set df$Timer,  but in this case test is not forced choice. Is it possible to save item response time in a forced choice test.
The observed response times should be saved automatically for each participant. Do you have an example where this isn't the case? Could be a bug worth looking into.
2- Some of items contain picture. I can add picture to item stem, as you show in github examples. But when I try to add picture in options, it does not work. Is it possible to add picture in options?

Easiest way to do this is probably via the shinyGUI list option choiceNames and choiceValue inputs. Here's an example using basic HTML type inputs, but of course you can point to images as well:

library(mirtCAT)
options <- matrix(c(1,2,3,4,5),
                  nrow = 3, ncol = 5, byrow = TRUE)
questions <- c("Building CATs with mirtCAT is difficult.",
               "mirtCAT requires a substantial amount of coding.",
               "I would use mirtCAT in my research.")
df <- data.frame(Question = questions, Option = options, Type = "radio")

choiceNames <- list(
    list(
        icon("calendar"),
        HTML("<p style='color:red;'>Red Text</p>"),
        "Normal text"),
    NULL, NULL
)
choiceValues = list(
    list("icon", "html", "text"), NULL, NULL)
results2 <- mirtCAT(df = df, shinyGUI = list(forced_choice = TRUE,
                                             choiceNames=choiceNames,
                                             choiceValues=choiceValues))


 

Thanks,

Levent
